summary.oneLiner: Q1FY27 opened strong (power-supply revenue +29%, EBITDA +33% at a 94% margin, energy sales +30%, 20 GW milestone crossed), but the defining change this quarter is strategic: AGEL is **de-risking its merchant/C&I exposure by contracting essentially all such capacity to sibling Adani Energy Solutions (AESL)** on 25-yr (solar/wind) and 15-yr (battery) fixed-price arm's-length PPAs. AGEL reframes itself as a pure execution/operational-excellence play chasing predictable ~15–16% IRRs, while BESS scales fast (3.5 GWh installed, 10+ GWh targeted this year).
summary.business: AGEL develops, owns and runs large-scale grid-connected solar, wind, hybrid, Battery Energy Storage Solution (BESS) and pumped-hydro storage plants, delivering renewable power and storage solutions at scale. It primarily serves B2B customers, principally State utilities and Distribution Companies (DISCOMs), under long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with DISCOMs and Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies, with roughly 78.4% of the portfolio backed by executed PPAs with sovereign counterparties such as SECI, PTC, NTPC and NHPC. The company also derives a smaller share of turnover from sale of solar power equipment.

currentContext.strengths: Scale and pace: India's largest renewable energy portfolio (19.3 GW operational as of Mar-2026) with 5.1 GW greenfield capacity added in FY26 — cited as the highest greenfield annual capacity expansion globally by any company excluding China.|Land and transmission lock-in: secures resource-rich land covering nearly 2,50,000 acres and locks in transmission access early, aligning design/engineering/supply chain to commission projects ahead of PPA timelines and deliver better IRRs.|O&M execution: analytics-based Operations & Maintenance via its Energy Network Operation Centre (ENOC) monitors all plants across 12 states in real time; solar plant availability above 99.2% and EBITDA margins above 90% maintained for five consecutive years.|Capital management discipline: matches debt tenure to PPA tenure to lower refinancing risk, drawing on a diversified funding pool of domestic banks/financial institutions, international lenders and global/local bond markets.|Technology edge: uses bifacial and n-type solar PV modules, horizontal single-axis trackers and India's largest 5.2 MW wind turbines to lower the Levelised Cost of Electricity (LCOE).|Revenue visibility: approximately 78.4% of the portfolio is backed by executed PPAs with sovereign counterparties (SECI, PTC, NTPC, NHPC, State DISCOMs).
currentContext.strategies: Shifting the operating model from self-execution to a partner-led model by engaging specialised EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) and O&M (Operations and Maintenance) partners, repositioning the internal workforce toward strategic governance and assurance to keep the organisation agile, scalable and resilient.|Focused on leveraging technology to reduce the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) in pursuit of enabling large-scale adoption of affordable clean energy.|People strategy centred on building a future-ready, inclusive and responsible workforce by strengthening skills, leadership and digital capabilities (including Agentic AI, robotic process automation and workforce analytics for demand forecasting and optimisation).|Cadre hiring strategy to build a robust pipeline of young engineering and management talent for cross-functional capability and long-term growth, supported by a Long Term Retention Bonus (LTRB) to retain top talent.|AGEL has not declared any dividend since incorporation, including for FY 2025-26 — the Board decided, after holistically considering the tremendous growth opportunities the Company is engaged with, that it would be prudent not to recommend a dividend for the year, and the Board also does not propose to transfer any amount to General Reserves, consistent with a reinvestment-led capital allocation philosophy governed by the Dividend Distribution and Shareholder Return Policy under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A.
currentContext.expansion: AGEL's flagship greenfield build-out is the Khavda Renewable Energy Park (Gujarat), described as the world's largest single-location renewable power plant under development; against a total planned installed capacity of 30 GW at Khavda, about 9.4 GW had been commissioned as of 31 March 2026, with the remaining capacity work-in-progress. Overall operational renewable capacity jumped 35% YoY to 19.3 GW in FY 2025-26 with a greenfield capacity addition of 5.1 GW (1.5x the FY 2024-25 addition), described as the highest greenfield annual capacity expansion globally by any company excluding China; this was achieved on a capex of ` 30,365 crore during the year. In energy storage, AGEL operationalised 1,376 MWh of BESS capacity at Khavda (installed capacity 1,579 MWh), one of the world's largest single-location BESS deployments, and intends to establish 10+ GWh of BESS capacity by March 2027, leveraging its large Khavda land bank. In pumped-hydro storage (PSP), AGEL has three projects with environmental clearance — Chitravathi (500 MW, Andhra Pradesh), Tarali (1,500 MW) and Gandikota (1,000 MW); Chitravathi, AGEL's first hydro PSP, spans 407 acres and is scheduled to be operational by FY 2026-27, generating over 1 TWh annually with about 6.2 hours per cycle. During the year AGEL also secured PPAs for 1,250 MW PSP capacity from Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd and 500 MW PSP capacity from Assam Power Distribution Company Limited, and works with five states toward a target of over 5 GW PSP capacity by 2030, on the path to AGEL's overall 50 GW renewable capacity target by 2030.
currentContext.mdna: Renewables are expected to overtake coal as the top global electricity source in 2026, reaching 36% of global power at 6,000+ TWh from wind and solar alone, framing a structural industry tailwind.|India's public capital expenditure reached ` 12.2 lakh crore, advancing infrastructure and stimulating manufacturing, construction and energy sectors, with the Union Budget 2026-27 continuing to prioritise energy transition among its priorities.|The Indian economy's outlook stays positive and stable, with real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 projected between 6.8% and 7.2%, supported by continued government infrastructure spending and rising private-sector investment.

risks.risk: Related-party transaction exposure within the Adani Group ecosystem
risks.note: The Company's RPT Policy exists specifically to manage 'potential or actual conflicts of interest' arising from transactions with related parties; all RPTs by the Company, and by subsidiaries exceeding their standalone turnover, are routed through Audit Committee review and, for material RPTs, shareholder approval, signalling a structurally significant related-party transaction base tied to the wider Adani Group.

risks.note: The MD&A's global economic outlook notes that growth projections hold only as 'risks from policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions persist,' a macro backdrop relevant to a capital-intensive, financing-dependent renewable energy developer with international lenders and bond-market exposure.

one-line thesis: Q1FY27 opened strong (power-supply revenue +29%, EBITDA +33% at a 94% margin, energy sales +30%, 20 GW milestone crossed), but the defining change this quarter is strategic: AGEL is **de-risking its merchant/C&I exposure by contracting essentially all such capacity to sibling Adani Energy Solutions (AESL)** on 25-yr (solar/wind) and 15-yr (battery) fixed-price arm's-length PPAs. AGEL reframes itself as a pure execution/operational-excellence play chasing predictable ~15–16% IRRs, while BESS scales fast (3.5 GWh installed, 10+ GWh targeted this year).

|---|---|---|---|

> One-off / distortion: **curtailment is currently a ~5–7% drag on overall EBITDA**; mgmt expects it to "weed out" (at least at Khavda) by end of CY2026 as transmission lines come online. Infirm/merchant power realised ~INR 2.5/unit.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** no explicit revenue guidance; run-rate EBITDA to rise from ~INR 17,000 cr to **~INR 21,000 cr by FY27-end**.
- **Margin:** 94% power-supply EBITDA margin sustained; BESS EBITDA thumb-rule **INR 25–30 lakh per MWh**.
- **Capacity add FY27: 5 GW** greenfield solar/wind/hybrid (explicitly **excludes** BESS and PSP).
- **BESS: 10+ GWh** cumulative this fiscal (from 3.5 GWh); **50 GWh by FY30** ambition.
- **PSP:** maiden **500 MW Chitravathi (AP)** to commission this financial year; 5 GW PSP target by 2030.
- **Capex FY27: ~INR 42,000 cr.**
- **Transmission/evacuation:** additional **7 GW by end CY2026**; balance of ~14 GW pipeline over the following quarter or two.
order book & pipeline:
- 20+ GW operational; Khavda (world's largest RE installation) >10 GW group solar/wind/hybrid operational.
- ~14 GW of evacuation capacity additions pending grid readiness (7 GW by end CY26).
- Virtually all merchant/C&I capacity now contracted to AESL; only direct-to-DISCOM (SECI-type) and temporarily-ahead-of-PPA infirm power sold by AGEL directly.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **AESL offtake structure:** solar/wind 25-yr fixed price (benchmark ~INR 2.7 / 3.4–3.5 per kWh), battery 15-yr fixed price, each project 25-yr arm's-length PPA on SECI standard terms, no termination-for-convenience; targets AGEL's ~15–16% hurdle IRR. Pricing set at market benchmark via Audit Committee (both listed entities).
- **BESS economics:** arbitrage model — charge ~INR 2.5, discharge INR 4–5 (INR ~4–5 spread) in evening peak; capex ~INR 1.5 cr/MWh; first 3.5 GWh contract fully capitalised by May-end. AGEL to start reporting BESS separately going forward.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Storage is the second engine:** BESS 3.5 → 10 GWh this year → 50 GWh by FY30; PSP entering via Chitravathi 500 MW.
- Evaluating other **Khavda-scale greenfield sites** (high-radiation locations) on the back of Khavda execution confidence.
- Rising AI/data-center power demand and RE+storage firming cited as structural tailwinds.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scale/execution moat:** AGEL is "virtually half of the total operational as well as battery-storage capacity in this country," heading to **more than two-thirds by year-end** — single-handedly defining India's grid-storage base.
- **Cost leadership:** 94% EBITDA margin on power supply; Khavda experience "phenomenally good," giving confidence to execute the next set of very large sites.
margins & cost dynamics:
- 94% power-supply EBITDA margin. Curtailment 5–7% EBITDA drag today, expected to fade by CY26-end.
- BESS: capex INR 1.5 cr/MWh, EBITDA INR 25–30 lakh/MWh; economics improve as more assets capitalise over the next nine months.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY27 capex ~INR 42,000 cr (≈5 GW RE + push to 10+ GWh BESS). Q1 capex INR 8,800 cr (+41% YoY).
- **Binding constraint is evacuation/transmission, not project execution** — new-project timing is now mapped to when evacuation is likely to come online.
capital allocation:
- The AESL contracting transfers merchant-tariff, ISTS/ALMM-waiver and market ups/downs (incl. the ~INR 0.50/unit transmission-cost arbitrage) **to AESL**; AGEL keeps predictable long-term returns.
- Continued reinvestment into greenfield + storage; no dividend/buyback (growth-stage IPP).
risks & watch-items:
- **Transmission/evacuation availability** is the explicit growth governor.
- **Related-party concentration:** near-all merchant/C&I offtake now with sibling AESL (arm's-length/Audit-Committee-approved, but material RPT optics).
- BESS execution at 10 GWh scale unproven; battery-fire risk — mgmt clarified a competitor's incident was a **PCS/IGBT (inverter) fire, not a battery fire**; projects carry standard insurance + Tier-1 OEMs.
- Falling solar tariffs (units +30% vs revenue +29% roughly matched this quarter) — realisation compression on newer vintages.
management quality / tone: Confident and leadership-framed; CEO Ashish Khanna fielded most questions and articulated the de-risking rationale clearly. Some specifics deflected ("benchmark rate" rather than exact per-kWh AESL pricing). Battery-storage CEO Rajat Seksaria credible on fire/insurance and unit economics.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Business-model pivot:** from a merchant-tariff/transmission-arbitrage builder to a fixed-return contracted IPP via AESL — materially lower risk, lower upside, cleaner cash flows. The ISTS/ALMM-waiver and INR 0.50/unit transmission arbitrage upside now sits with AESL.
- The read-through of "grid, not panels, is the bottleneck" points straight at **transmission capex (AESL)** as the group's actual growth governor.
- AGEL ≈ India's entire grid-battery base today; first-mover scale advantage but also concentration risk.
- PSP (ex-Chitravathi) is still ~2 years out — storage growth near-term is BESS-led.

- 20+ GW operational; Khavda (world's largest RE installation) >10 GW group solar/wind/hybrid operational.
- ~14 GW of evacuation capacity additions pending grid readiness (7 GW by end CY26).
- Virtually all merchant/C&I capacity now contracted to AESL; only direct-to-DISCOM (SECI-type) and temporarily-ahead-of-PPA infirm power sold by AGEL directly.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **AESL offtake structure:** solar/wind 25-yr fixed price (benchmark ~INR 2.7 / 3.4–3.5 per kWh), battery 15-yr fixed price, each project 25-yr arm's-length PPA on SECI standard terms, no termination-for-convenience; targets AGEL's ~15–16% hurdle IRR. Pricing set at market benchmark via Audit Committee (both listed entities).
- **BESS economics:** arbitrage model — charge ~INR 2.5, discharge INR 4–5 (INR ~4–5 spread) in evening peak; capex ~INR 1.5 cr/MWh; first 3.5 GWh contract fully capitalised by May-end. AGEL to start reporting BESS separately going forward.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Storage is the second engine:** BESS 3.5 → 10 GWh this year → 50 GWh by FY30; PSP entering via Chitravathi 500 MW.
- Evaluating other **Khavda-scale greenfield sites** (high-radiation locations) on the back of Khavda execution confidence.
- Rising AI/data-center power demand and RE+storage firming cited as structural tailwinds.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scale/execution moat:** AGEL is "virtually half of the total operational as well as battery-storage capacity in this country," heading to **more than two-thirds by year-end** — single-handedly defining India's grid-storage base.
- **Cost leadership:** 94% EBITDA margin on power supply; Khavda experience "phenomenally good," giving confidence to execute the next set of very large sites.
margins & cost dynamics:
- 94% power-supply EBITDA margin. Curtailment 5–7% EBITDA drag today, expected to fade by CY26-end.
- BESS: capex INR 1.5 cr/MWh, EBITDA INR 25–30 lakh/MWh; economics improve as more assets capitalise over the next nine months.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY27 capex ~INR 42,000 cr (≈5 GW RE + push to 10+ GWh BESS). Q1 capex INR 8,800 cr (+41% YoY).
- **Binding constraint is evacuation/transmission, not project execution** — new-project timing is now mapped to when evacuation is likely to come online.
capital allocation:
- The AESL contracting transfers merchant-tariff, ISTS/ALMM-waiver and market ups/downs (incl. the ~INR 0.50/unit transmission-cost arbitrage) **to AESL**; AGEL keeps predictable long-term returns.
- Continued reinvestment into greenfield + storage; no dividend/buyback (growth-stage IPP).
risks & watch-items:
- **Transmission/evacuation availability** is the explicit growth governor.
- **Related-party concentration:** near-all merchant/C&I offtake now with sibling AESL (arm's-length/Audit-Committee-approved, but material RPT optics).
- BESS execution at 10 GWh scale unproven; battery-fire risk — mgmt clarified a competitor's incident was a **PCS/IGBT (inverter) fire, not a battery fire**; projects carry standard insurance + Tier-1 OEMs.
- Falling solar tariffs (units +30% vs revenue +29% roughly matched this quarter) — realisation compression on newer vintages.
management quality / tone: Confident and leadership-framed; CEO Ashish Khanna fielded most questions and articulated the de-risking rationale clearly. Some specifics deflected ("benchmark rate" rather than exact per-kWh AESL pricing). Battery-storage CEO Rajat Seksaria credible on fire/insurance and unit economics.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Business-model pivot:** from a merchant-tariff/transmission-arbitrage builder to a fixed-return contracted IPP via AESL — materially lower risk, lower upside, cleaner cash flows. The ISTS/ALMM-waiver and INR 0.50/unit transmission arbitrage upside now sits with AESL.
- The read-through of "grid, not panels, is the bottleneck" points straight at **transmission capex (AESL)** as the group's actual growth governor.
- AGEL ≈ India's entire grid-battery base today; first-mover scale advantage but also concentration risk.
- PSP (ex-Chitravathi) is still ~2 years out — storage growth near-term is BESS-led.
